Over the workspace Λ n ( κ ) varies only 1 . 4 × , i.e. ρ ∈ [0 . 70 , 1 . 0] , a margin of more than 3 × to ρ ⋆ ≈ 3 . 4 ( Λ n, true > 0 . 29 Λ n, ref ); under-estimates ( Λ n, true > Λ n, ref , ρ < 1 ) are always stable since ρ ⋆ > 1 . blocks.block_content: The primary value of prediction here is interaction- constraint enforcement and trajectory feedforward , not contact-force forecasting: the feedforward ¨ p d and the known constraint bounds are exact, the Kalman disturbance estimate moderate, and force prediction near-useless (the tissue is unknown). A zero-order-hold ˆ d ( k + i ) = ˆ d ( k ) is therefore adopted, and the offset-free guarantee holds at steady state regardless of prediction quality. This integrating model is a worst-case approximation for any slowly-varying distur- bance; the ∼ 1 Hz cardiac force could instead be predicted by (A) raising the process-noise covariance for faster adaptation, or (B) an ECG-gated periodic model ˆ d ( k +1) = ˆ d DC ( k ) + A card sin( ω heart ( k +1)∆ t + ϕ ) —left to future work. During first contact the estimate lags a few samples; the hard force constraint is the safety backstop in that transient.

blocks.block_content: We evaluate the controller on a distributed-compliance plant in the MuJoCo physics engine: an eight-link pseudo-rigid- body (PRB) tendon-driven catheter (each joint a torsional spring approximating the segment flexural rigidity, total length 5 cm), actuated through a routed spatial tendon (tension- only), pressing on a Kelvin–Voigt tissue wall ( k t = 5 kN/m, b t = 40 N · s/m, applied analytically on the tip so the stiff contact is faithful—MuJoCo’s regularized soft contact cannot represent it). This plant genuinely violates the reduced-order assumptions: eight elastic DOFs, a configuration-dependent tendon transmission, and distributed bending the scalar model lumps away. The scalar operational-space inertia Λ n ( κ ) and tendon-to-tip-normal transmission J n ( κ ) are read from the model (mass matrix and tip Jacobian on the contact nor- mal): Λ n ≈ 3 . 5 × 10 − 3 , J n ≈ 0 . 087 , catheter tip stiffness k eff ≈ 8 . 4 N/m. Two specializations carry the scalar design onto this plant: the impedance gains are Λ n -scaled to the measured inertia (preserving ω ≈ 30 rad/s), and the corrective force F mpc is realized in tendon space , T = − ( u ff + F mpc ) /J n with Layer-1 feedforward u ff = k eff y d , so the hard bound (13) is the box | F mpc | ≤ F safe on the corrective force (the elastic k eff e contribution to ˆ F n is negligible on the compliant catheter). By Theorem 1 the unconstrained controller is the static impedance feedback and the scalar force-magnitude QP reduces to the predicted-force clip used here; the offset- free disturbance is an integrating estimator on the tip error. Control rate 500 Hz; tendon limit ± 8 N; F safe = 0 . 5 N. The reference approaches the surface (1 s), presses to a target 1.5 mm past it ( ≈ 7 . 5 N if tracked rigidly—far beyond what an 8 N tendon delivers through J n ), holds 1 s, and retracts, deliberately stressing the safety mechanism. Reproducible: simulation/catheter_benchmark_mujoco.py .
